guitar.evidence: 90s jangle-pop band, guitarists used typical Fender guitars; not strongly documented as iconic.

tone.target: jangly Vox/Fender edge-of-breakup pop rock with light chorus
tone.profile: jangly Vox/Fender edge-of-breakup pop rock with light chorus
tone.summary: A classic pop-rock jangle tone achieved using a Fender/Vox style amp (US Deluxe/AC30 TB), light compression for sustain, and Chorus for the signature shimmer. The signal chain emphasizes brightness and clarity.
corrections: shift from generic indie rock to 90s pop-rock jangle

rig.name: Gin Blossoms - Hey Jealousy - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Add sustain and even out the dynamic range for arpeggios.
Provide the necessary edge-of-breakup grit without heavy fuzz.
blocks.gap: The Green OD is chosen for its classic, non-aggressive breakup character, mimicking a slightly pushed tube amp.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative if the desired grit is slightly warmer.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the bright, clean Fender/Vox character required for pop-rock jangle.
Provide a bright, articulate sound suitable for single-coil guitars and arpeggios.
Add the signature subtle shimmer and width required for 90s pop-rock jangle.
blocks.gap: The settings are dialed back to ensure a subtle, non-lush effect.

blocks.purpose: Enhance the high-end sparkle and cut any muddy low frequencies.
Provide a subtle sense of space and depth without sounding overly wet.
Optional: Used for specific rhythmic accents; kept off by default to maintain clarity.
blocks.gap: Not strictly necessary, but included as a versatile option.

improvements.summary: Upgrade the cabinet IR for more authentic Vox AC30 character to enhance jangle tone.

proposals.reason: The US 2x12 is too American; a Vox cab will nail the jangle tone.
